source: WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record - Cholera in 1977 (WER 53(17):117-118)
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 1977-01-01..1977-12-31. The table is headed 'Country/Area - Pays/Territoire' and does list non-sovereign territories in their own right (Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands, Guam, Hong Kong, Macao, Gaza), so a territory with cholera would have been expected to appear. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: in this period the territory was South West Africa under South African administration (independence 1990-03-21), it was not a WHO Member State, and any cases could in principle have been folded into the South Africa line or not notified at all - hence the reduced confidence (0.6) and surveillance status 'partial' rather than 'operational'. Honesty caveat recorded by WHO itself: the WER annual reports of this era note that 'several additional countries could be considered also to be infected on the basis of earlier reports and information from other sources', so underreporting cannot be excluded. Evidence type: Inferred_Absence. National-level row; no sub-national rows exist for this period.
